chunks: From him, from Muhammad ibn Isa, from Al-Dahqan, from Durust, from Ibrahim ibn Abd al-Hamid, from Abu al-Hasan (peace be upon him), who said:

From what Adam (peace be upon him) bequeathed to Hibatullah was that he said to him: 'Upon you is the pomegranate, for if you eat it while you are hungry, it will suffice you, and if you eat it while you are satiated, it will order you (for more food).'
ai.seo_question: What is the spiritual or physical significance of eating pomegranates according to Shia hadith?
ai.summary: Recorded in *Al-Kafi*’s chapter on the virtues of fruits, this hadith traces its chain back to Imam al-Sadiq (peace be upon him), linking the wisdom of the first human, Adam, to the Imams' teachings. It highlights the pomegranate's unique physiological balance, serving as both a sufficient meal for the hungry and an appetite stimulant for the satiated, reflecting the divine wisdom embedded in creation.

en.hubeali:
From him, from Muhammad Bin Isa, from Al Dahqan, from Dorost, from Ibrahim Bin Abdul Hameed, 
(It has been narrated) from Abu Al-Hassan<sup>asws</sup> having said:

‘From what Adam<sup>as</sup> bequeathed with to Hibtullah<sup>as</sup> was that he<sup>as</sup> said to him<sup>as</sup>: ‘It is upon you with (eating) the Pomegranate, for if you<sup>as</sup> were to eat it and you<sup>as</sup> are hungry so it would suffice you<sup>as</sup>, and if you<sup>as</sup> were to eat it and you<sup>as</sup> are satiated, it would order you (for more food)’.
en.sarwar: 4. It is narrated from the narrator of the previous Hadith from Muhammad ibn ‘Isa from al-Dihqan from Durust from Ibrahim ibn ‘Abd al-Hamid who has said the following: “Abu al-Hassan, ‘Alayhi al-Salam, has said,

‘Of the matters that Adam said in his will to Hibbatu Allah was his saying, ‘You must eat pomegranate; if you eat it when you are hungry, it is sufficient; and if you eat when satisfied it is pleasant to you.’”
